recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future rendered page lacks the Period constraints table, investigate the datatype macro or publisher output rather than changing the current source inputs.
issue_request: FHIR-39320 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction, raised against R4 and applied for R5, asking that the Period datatype page include a Constraints table like Range and RatioRange because Period has a Structure-tab rule that start SHALL be lower than end.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-39320 was found for source/datatypes.html or source/datatypes/period.xml. Commit d621ab0bda61832d87d16ee8fa98261bf403a9da, made before this Jira was created, uncommented the Period constraints block in source/datatypes.html and thereby enabled the existing [%dt.constraints Period%] publisher macro.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini maps general data types to source/datatypes.html, so the inspected Period section is in current build scope. source/datatypes/period.xml defines the Period Start <= End invariant, and R5/current rendered datatypes pages include the generated constraint text. FHIR-20652 surfaced in broad Jira search but concerns older Timing.repeat period/frequency description wording and does not conflict with the base Period constraint table. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant contradictory discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already contains the Period Constraints section and the authoritative Period spreadsheet already contains the invariant that section renders.

related_jiras.note: Older Published issue about duplicated Timing.repeat period/frequency description text; it surfaced in Period/Constraints Jira search but does not govern the base Period constraints table.
